subject: Did you already automate multiple MCDS analyses through R or Python

messages.author: 56a7c973f6806d17
messages.subject: Did you already automate multiple MCDS analyses through R or Python
parts:
Hello all.

I'm here in behalf of a little team of french birders from the Auvergne LPO who've been using Distance 6.2
for around 3 years now for at least 3 multi-species studies
(if you read french, see https://distancesampling.blogspot.fr/p/un-collectif-dornithologues.html).

We have been using the MCDS engine for estimating the populations of birds of around 25 species,
with some tens of line transects and around 300 points transects, so it's quite a lot of work,
achieved til now with the great Distance 6.2 sofware.

Now, after using the limited (AFAWK) automation features of Distance, we are willing to go
one step further and run our analyses more automatically, at least to do a first auto-sorting
of the "best" models and "best" truncation distances (left and right side)

(very roughly said, something like auto-running analyses for "all" combinations of models and left/right
 truncation values, and then sort-out the "best" analyses from some criteria like AIC, Chi2, KSp ... etc)

We know that this is possible through programming with the R language / infrastructure,
thanks to Distance-specific R modules, and this is great !

But we'd like to know :
* if some of you have already achieved this kind of programming work,
* if so, if you'd be ready to share your code,
* if some of you have already worked on the same target, but using Python
  (there's no Distance interface to this language, but it's quite straightforward to code,
   as it's only about running MCDS.exe and reading/writing Distance output/input files)

Thanks in advance fro your help.

Jean-Philippe.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Did you already automate multiple MCDS analyses through R or Python
parts:
Hi Jean-Philippe, hi listfolk,

This kind of approach is possible using the Distance package in R. You
might be interested in a poster that we (myself, Eric Rexstad, Lindesay
Scott-Hayward) put together a few years ago on "Convenient analysis of
numerous distance sampling data sets in R"

http://converged.yt/posters/Rexstad-ISEC2014.pdf

In practice these kind of analyses seem to work fairly well, though the
model checking can be somewhat arduous. You may be particularly
interested in the function summarize_ds_models() in Distance.


Hope this helps!


cheers,
--dave
